classification.difficultyReason: Students equate the derivative to the supplied gradient, recover the point using logarithms and substitution, then construct its tangent equation.

content.prompt: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y=3e^x+x$ with gradient $2.5$.

answer.short:
$y=\dfrac52x+\dfrac32\ln2+\dfrac32$

Set $y'=\frac52$ to locate the point, then use the point and gradient.
answer.worked:
Since $y'=3e^x+1$, set the derivative equal to $\frac52$.
$$\begin{align*}
3e^x+1&=\frac52\\
3e^x&=\frac32\\
e^x&=\frac12\\
x&=-\ln2
\end{align*}$$
At this point,
$$\begin{align*}
y&=3e^{-\ln2}-\ln2\\
y&=\frac32-\ln2
\end{align*}$$
Using the point $(-\ln2,\frac32-\ln2)$ and gradient $\frac52$, the tangent is
$$\begin{align*}
y-\left(\frac32-\ln2\right)&=\frac52(x+\ln2)\\
y&=\frac52x+\frac32\ln2+\frac32
\end{align*}$$
